The Swift SDK's SwiftUI kit. One modifier gates an iPhone or iPad app and runs every screen the
license needs: Welcome, the one sign-in form, the key field with its live verdict, Replace a
device, the blocking states with their fixes, offline grace and the toast. On iOS and iPadOS 26
the controls are Liquid Glass; on 18 the same layout runs on system materials. Every screen is
drawn from **PolarisKeyUICore**, a SwiftUI-free presentation core that runs the shared
[UI state matrix](/docs/reference/corpus/) for every component, so a UIKit app or a UI of your
own gets the same states, copy and actions. The rest of the Swift SDK is on the
[Swift](/docs/build/sdks/swift/) page; the Mac pass of the kit follows.

<KitFacts kit="swiftui" />

## Install

The kit is two products of the `polaris-key.PolarisKey` package in Polaris Key's Swift registry
([Installing the SDKs from the feeds](/docs/build/install-from-feeds/)). The package's floors are
iOS 18, macOS 15, tvOS 18 and visionOS 2.

```swift
dependencies: [
    .package(id: "polaris-key.PolarisKey", from: "0.1.0")
],
targets: [
    .target(name: "MyApp", dependencies: [
        .product(name: "PolarisKeyUI", package: "polaris-key.PolarisKey"),      // the views
        .product(name: "PolarisKeyUICore", package: "polaris-key.PolarisKey"),  // no SwiftUI
    ])
]
```

The kit bundles Rubik and JetBrains Mono (both OFL) and registers them itself.

## The one-line flow

```swift
import PolarisKeyUI

WindowGroup { ContentView().polarisKeyGate(client) }
```

`.polarisKeyGate` starts the client, shows the product's icon until the first check answers (never
the sign-in screen during a cached-session check), re-renders on `client.events` and refreshes when
the scene becomes active. It takes `KitGateOptions` for what the build offers (key entry, offline
activation, a trial) and how sign-in presents (`signInPresentation: .inline`, the default, or
`.sheet`; `replace: .inline` or `.browser`). An app that opens sign-in from its own menu uses the
sheet:

```swift
.polarisKeySignIn(isPresented: $signingIn, model: model)
```

## Piecemeal

Every screen and part is public and takes the core's `KitScreen` for its component, so it can sit
anywhere inside `PolarisKeyScope(model:)`, which puts the resolved theme, copy and product icon in
the environment:

- screens: `BootView`, `WelcomeView`, `ActivateView`, `SignInView` (with its steps
  `SignInMethodsView`, `SignInHandoffView`, `LicenseChoiceView`, `ReplaceDeviceView`),
  `DeviceLimitView`, `StatusScreenView`, `GraceBannerView`, `UpdatePromptView`,
  `UpdateProgressView`, `ReleaseNotesView`, `PaywallView`, `EntitlementGate` and `ToastView`;
- panes for your own settings `Form`: `AccountAndLicenseSection`, `DevicesSection` and
  `SettingsSection`;
- parts: `ProductIcon`, `MonogramIcon`, `ProductHeader`, `KeyField`, `CodeDisplay`,
  `CountdownRing`, `SeatMeter`, `DeviceRow`, `StatusPill`, `LoadingIndicator`, `ProgressBar` and
  `PoweredBy`.

A `PolarisKeyStyle` replaces or wraps one component's body the way a `ButtonStyle` does, with the
component's state, copy lines and actions in its configuration:

```swift
struct MyWelcome: PolarisKeyStyle {
    func makeBody(configuration: PolarisKeyStyleConfiguration) -> some View {
        VStack {
            Text(configuration.text("welcome.title") ?? "")
            configuration.content   // the kit's own Welcome, below your header
        }
    }
}

ContentView().polarisKeyGate(client).welcomeStyle(MyWelcome())
```

## Headless

`PolarisKeyUICore` imports no SwiftUI. `PolarisKeyGateModel` is an `@Observable` view of the client
as `KitInputs`, with the actions every screen needs (`submitKey()`, `beginSignIn()`,
`reopenBrowser()`, `useCode()`, `cancelSignIn()`, `useDifferentKey()`, `signOut()`, `refresh()`).
`KitStates` holds one pure function per component from `KitInputs` to a `KitScreen` (its state, its
copy lines with their arguments, and its actions); `KitCopy` formats a line in any launch locale.
A UI of your own binds to the model, or fills `KitInputs` from its own state and calls `KitStates`.

```swift
let screen = KitStates.activate(model.inputs)
switch screen.state {
case .parsed: Text(KitCopy.bundled.format(screen.line("part.keyField.forProduct")!, locale: "en"))
case .deviceLimit: /* the neutral callout, and Replace a device */
default: EmptyView()
}
```

`PolarisKeyPreviewState.all` names a fixture input for every state, for `#Preview`s and your own
tests: `PolarisKeyPreview(.named(.welcome, "default")!)` draws one; `PolarisKeyGallery()` lists
them all.

The product's identity comes from your theme, then the product's registered presentation through
the SDK's presentation source, then the app bundle; with no icon the kit draws a monogram, never a
Polaris Key mark.

## Theming

`.polarisKeyTheme(PolarisKeyTheme(…))` sets every field of the [theme](/docs/build/ui/theming/):
`preset` (`.polarisKey`, or `.native` for the system fonts, the app's tint and the system grounds),
`colorScheme`, `accent` (`.product`, `.core` or `.color("#…")`, always through the contrast
resolver), `radius`, `typography` (Rubik by default, `.system`, or a family you register),
`density`, `motion`, `ambient`, `product`, `copy`, `locale` and `poweredBy`.

## Localisation

The kit reads the generated catalog in nine locales from `PolarisKeyUICore`'s `kit-copy.json`,
formatted by the core (plurals, the form factor's word: "this iPhone", "this iPad"). `copy` in the
theme overrides a key per locale, falling back key by key: the locale's override, the locale's
table, the English override, then English.

## Sample

`examples/ui/swiftui/` is Tidewater Studio as an XcodeGen app: with no arguments it lists every
preview state; `-pkeyState Welcome.default` draws one; `--live` gates a list of sessions with
`.polarisKeyGate` against a real Worker (`PKEY_PRODUCT`, `PKEY_BASE_URL` and the pins in
`PKEY_PINS`). Its `run.sh` renders every state on the iOS simulator, runs
`performAccessibilityAudit` on each render and compares it with the committed baselines.
